evidence.intree_statement: Definition PreservesAllLimits {C D : Category} (F : C ⟶ D) : Type := ∀ (J : Category) (G : J ⟶ C), PreservesLimit G F.
Definition PreservesAllColimits {C D : Category} (F : C ⟶ D) : Type := ∀ (J : Category) (G : J ⟶ C), PreservesColimit G F.

Definition PreservesImageLimit : Type := ∀ (J : Category) (G : J ⟶ C) (L : Limit G) (N : Cone (U ◯ G)), ∃! φ : vertex_obj[N] ~{D}~> U L, ∀ x : J, image_leg L x ∘ φ ≈ cone_leg N x.   (* the cone-level, image-cone-universal reading of 'U is continuous' *)

statement_record.book: Naming definition in running prose: a functor that preserves limits is called continuous; a functor that preserves colimits is called cocontinuous. Used as the standing hypothesis of Theorems 4.7.3, 4.7.10, 4.7.15, 4.7.17.
statement_record.intree: PreservesAllLimits F := ∀ (J : Category) (G : J ⟶ C), PreservesLimit G F  /  PreservesAllColimits F := ∀ J G, PreservesColimit G F  /  PreservesImageLimit (for a fixed U) := ∀ J G L N, ∃! φ, ∀ x, image_leg L x ∘ φ ≈ cone_leg N x
statement_record.strength_comparison: same for the naming content, but the two forms differ in strength and the file says so itself. PreservesAllLimits is built on the APEX-ONLY class PreservesLimit (Preservation.v:48, `preserves_limit (L : Limit G) : IsALimit (F ◯ G) (F L)`), which only asserts that the apex object F L carries SOME limit structure, whose legs need not be the image legs — strictly weaker than the book's 'F carries the limit cone to a limit cone'. The correct cone-level reading is in-tree as PreservesImageLimit (Comma/Limit.v:110), which is exactly the book's notion and is what GAFT/SAFT actually consume; it is stated per-functor and quantified over all diagram shapes, so it IS 'U is continuous' in the book's sense, just not carrying that name. The COCONTINUOUS clause exists only in the apex-only form (PreservesAllColimits, defined by duality from PreservesColimit); there is no cone-level cocontinuity in-tree. No smallness restriction on J, so 'preserves all (small) limits' is rendered as 'preserves limits of every shape', which universe polymorphism makes the honest reading.

evidence.intree_statement: Definition Comma_Complete (HU : PreservesImageLimit) (HC : @Complete C) : @Complete (=(d) ↓ U) := fun J K => comma_limit HC HU K.

Definition comma_limit : Limit K := @Build_Limit J (=(d) ↓ U) K apex_cone comma_ump.   (* apex_obj := ((ttt, vertex_obj[Ldiag]); phi) with Ldiag := HC J (comma_proj2 ◯ K) and apex_leg j the projected C-legs — the comma limit lies over the C-limit of the projected diagram, which is the creation content *)

Definition Comma_Complete_right_adjoint {C D : Category} {F : D ⟶ C} {U : C ⟶ D} (A : F ⊣ U) (d : D) (HC : @Complete C) : @Complete (=(d) ↓ U) := Comma_Complete (right_adjoint_PreservesImageLimit A) HC.

statement_record.book: For any U : A → S and any s ∈ S, the forgetful functor Π : s ↓ U → A STRICTLY CREATES the limit of any diagram whose limit exists in A and is preserved by U. In particular, if A is complete and U is continuous then s ↓ U is complete.
statement_record.intree: Comma_Complete (HU : PreservesImageLimit) (HC : @Complete C) : @Complete (=(d) ↓ U); the underlying comma_limit builds the limit of K : J ⟶ (=(d) ↓ U) with apex ((ttt, Ldiag); φ), Ldiag the C-limit of comma_proj2 ◯ K and φ the mediator into the preserved image cone, legs the projected C-legs.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker in FORM. The 'in particular' clause is present verbatim and in full (Comma_Complete), with the preservation hypothesis taken at the correct cone level (PreservesImageLimit). But the primary statement — per-diagram STRICT CREATION by the projection Π = comma_proj2 — is not asserted: the in-tree hypotheses are global (C complete, U image-preserving for ALL diagrams) rather than 'this one diagram has a limit in A that U preserves', and no lemma states that the projection creates (i.e. that the lift of a given A-limit cone to s ↓ U exists uniquely and is limiting).

gap: Two precise gaps. (1) No CREATION statement: the tree has no `Creates`/`CreatesLimits` predicate for comma projections and never asserts the uniqueness-of-lift half — comma_limit merely CONSTRUCTS a limit; that its projection is the given A-limit is visible in the term (apex_obj = ((ttt, Ldiag); φ)) but is not the content of any lemma. (Contrast Monad/Monadicity/Beck.v:164 CreatesUSplitCoequalizers, which does state creation, but only for U-split coequalizers, and Theory/Equivalence/Limit.v:486 equivalence_creates_limits, for equivalences.) (2) No per-diagram form: comma_limit/Comma_Complete require the global `@Complete C` and the global `PreservesImageLimit U`, so 'the limit of any diagram whose limit exists in A and is preserved by U' cannot be instantiated for a single diagram.

evidence.intree_statement: Theorem GAFT {C D : Category} (U : C ⟶ D) (comp : @Complete C) (cont : @PreservesImageLimit C D U) (sols : forall d : D, SolutionSet U d) : { F : D ⟶ C & F ⊣ U }.

Record SolutionSet {C D : Category} (U : C ⟶ D) (d : D) := { sol_index : Type; sol_obj : sol_index -> C; sol_arr : forall i, d ~> U (sol_obj i); sol_covers {c} (h : d ~> U c) : { i : sol_index & { t : sol_obj i ~> c & fmap[U] t ∘ sol_arr i ≈ h } } }.

Definition wif_of_sols {C D : Category} (U : C ⟶ D) (d : D) (S : SolutionSet U d) : WeaklyInitialFamily (=(d) ↓ U).   (* the book's parenthetical 'the solution set condition says exactly that {f_i} is a jointly weakly initial set in s ↓ U' *)

statement_record.book: Let U : A → S be continuous with A locally small and complete. If U satisfies the solution set condition — for every s ∈ S a SET of arrows Φ_s = {f_i : s → Ua_i} through which every f : s → Ua factors as f = Uk ∘ f_i — then U admits a left adjoint.
statement_record.intree: GAFT U (comp : @Complete C) (cont : @PreservesImageLimit C D U) (sols : forall d : D, SolutionSet U d) : { F : D ⟶ C & F ⊣ U }.  Proof: Comma_Complete makes =(d) ↓ U complete, wif_of_sols turns the solution set into a WeaklyInitialFamily there, initial_from_weakly_initial produces the initial object, GAFT_from_initials concludes.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. Every hypothesis matches: continuity is the cone-level PreservesImageLimit (the correct reading of the book's 'continuous', stronger than the apex-only class and documented as such in the file header); completeness of the domain is `@Complete C`; the solution set is the book's Φ_s with the factorization f = Uk ∘ f_i spelled as `fmap[U] t ∘ sol_arr i ≈ h`. Local smallness is not a separate hypothesis — hom-setoids already live at a fixed hom universe and the theorem is universe-polymorphic, and the place the book uses local smallness (forming the product over Hom(s↓U)) is exactly where the in-tree proof draws its endomorphism-indexed product from Comma_Complete. Two constructive rephrasings, both hypothesis-side (so no weakening of the conclusion): sol_index is a `Type` rather than 'a set' (smallness is caller-chosen via the universe of that Type), and sol_covers delivers the factorizing index and arrow as DATA (Σ-type) rather than as a bare existential.

statement_record.book: If C is complete, locally small, and has a jointly weakly initial SET of objects Φ, then C has an initial object. (Proof: take the limit l of the full subcategory spanned by Φ, exhibit a cone λ : l ⇒ id_C by a pullback argument, and conclude by the 'initial = limit of the identity' lemma 3.7.1.)
statement_record.intree: initial_from_weakly_initial: a WeaklyInitialFamily W, plus the product P of the family, plus the product Pe of the product object indexed by ITS OWN endomorphism hom-type, plus binary equalizers, yield @Initial C.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger (leaner hypotheses, same conclusion). All three limit inputs are consequences of `@Complete C`, so the in-tree lemma applies wherever the book's does, and additionally in categories that are not complete. Local smallness is discharged the same way the book uses it: the second product Pe is indexed by the hom-TYPE of endomorphisms of the first product, which is small exactly because homs are setoids at a fixed universe (the file header says the explicit form is chosen precisely to leave that smallness in the caller's hands). The PROOF is Freyd's product-then-equalize rather than Riehl's limit-over-Φ-plus-pullback, and the initial object is obtained directly as a Build_Terminal in C^op rather than via 'initial = limit of the identity'; the statement is unaffected.

evidence.intree_statement: Record SubObj {C : Category} (x : C) := { sub_dom : C; sub_mono : sub_dom ~> x; sub_is_monic : Monic sub_mono }.

#[export] Program Instance SubObj_Setoid : Setoid (SubObj x) := {| equiv := fun u v => { i : sub_dom u ≅ sub_dom v & sub_mono v ∘ to i ≈ sub_mono u } |}.   (* the book's 'isomorphic subobjects are typically identified', carried by the setoid equivalence itself *)
Theorem sub_equiv_iff_mutual (u v : SubObj x) : (u ≈ v) ↔ (sub_le u v * sub_le v u).

statement_record.book: A SUBOBJECT of c ∈ C is a monomorphism c' ↣ c with codomain c. Isomorphic subobjects — c' ↣ c ↢ c'' related by a commuting isomorphism c' ≅ c'' — are typically identified.
statement_record.intree: Record SubObj {C} (x : C) := { sub_dom : C; sub_mono : sub_dom ~> x; sub_is_monic : Monic sub_mono }, with SubObj_Setoid making u ≈ v mean { i : sub_dom u ≅ sub_dom v & sub_mono v ∘ to i ≈ sub_mono u }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, both clauses. The record is exactly 'a mono into x', and the identification of isomorphic subobjects is not left informal — it IS the setoid equivalence on SubObj x (the file header: 'the setoid structure itself carries the quotient'), the canonical setoid-library rendering of the book's quotient. sub_equiv_iff_mutual additionally proves that this identification coincides with mutual factorization in the factorization preorder sub_le, which the book only gestures at.

aliases: SAFT / Freyd special adjoint functor theorem

evidence.intree_statement: Definition SAFT {C D : Category} (U : C ⟶ D) (comp : @Complete C) (cont : @PreservesImageLimit C D U) (G : Cogenerator C) (WP : forall x : C, SubobjectIndex x) (cover : SubobjectCover U comp G WP) : { F : D ⟶ C & F ⊣ U } := GAFT U comp cont (SAFT_solution_set U comp G WP cover).

Definition SAFT_solution_set {C D : Category} (U : C ⟶ D) (comp : @Complete C) (G : Cogenerator C) (WP : forall x : C, SubobjectIndex x) (cover : SubobjectCover U comp G WP) (d : D) : SolutionSet U d.   (* members are the pairs (i, s) of a well-powered subobject of the cogenerator product and an arrow d ~> U (sub_dom i) *)

Lemma cogenerator_canonical_monic {C : Category} (comp : @Complete C) (G : Cogenerator C) (c : C) : Monic (cogen_canonical comp G c).   (* the one classical half proved internally: separation ⇒ the canonical map into the power of the cogenerating family is monic *)

statement_record.book: Let U : A → S be continuous with A complete and both A and S locally small. If A has a SMALL COSEPARATING SET and every collection of subobjects of a fixed object of A admits an INTERSECTION, then U admits a left adjoint. (Proof: each s ↓ U is locally small and complete, monos there are created by Π, a coseparating set for A gives one for s ↓ U, and Lemma 4.7.11 supplies the initial object.)
statement_record.intree: SAFT U (comp : @Complete C) (cont : @PreservesImageLimit C D U) (G : Cogenerator C) (WP : forall x, SubobjectIndex x) (cover : SubobjectCover U comp G WP) : { F : D ⟶ C & F ⊣ U }, where SubobjectCover U comp G WP := ∀ d c (h : d ~> U c), { i : sub_index (WP (cogen_prod comp G)) & { s : d ~> U (sub_dom … i) & { t : sub_dom … i ~> c & fmap[U] t ∘ s ≈ h } } }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the conclusion is the full left adjoint the book claims, but the hypothesis list carries an EXTRA input, `cover`, which is (pointwise) the CONCLUSION of the classical image-factorization step rather than a premise of the book's theorem. Continuity is at the correct cone level (PreservesImageLimit) and completeness matches; the coseparating set is Cogenerator (see riehl:4.7:def7); well-poweredness is packaged as data (SubobjectIndex x: a Type of indices, a domain and a mono into x for each). The file states this deviation openly: the size argument 'the subobjects of the cogenerator product form a set, and the image of h lands in one of them' cannot be run because the library has no smallness machinery and no image factorization on a general base.

gap: Three precise gaps against the book's statement. (1) The image-factorization step is ASSUMED, not derived: `cover : SubobjectCover U comp G WP` is an extra hypothesis stating exactly what the classical proof concludes (every h : d ~> U c factors through a subobject of the cogenerator product), so the theorem as stated is the book's theorem MINUS its hardest step. (2) The book's second hypothesis — every collection of subobjects of a fixed object admits an INTERSECTION — has no in-tree counterpart at all (see riehl:4.7:def9, ABSENT); it is replaced by the different hypothesis of well-poweredness-as-data (SubobjectIndex), and the monic annotation `sub_monic` is inert (SAFT.v:70-72 says the existence proof does not consume it). (3) The comma-category half of the book's proof — that Π : s ↓ U → A creates monos and intersections and transports a coseparating set of A to one of s ↓ U, and Lemma 4.7.11 producing the initial object from a coseparating set plus intersections — is not formalized; the in-tree route detours through GAFT and the solution set instead. What IS internalized in full is the separation ⇒ monic half (cogenerator_canonical_monic).
